enrichment.headline: Accepts a $75,000 Alta Bates Summit grant to fund the district's youth violence prevention program
enrichment.summary: The district accepts a $75,000 grant from Sutter Bay Hospitals, doing business as Alta Bates Summit Medical Center. The money pays for the Violence Prevention Program, which has a dedicated program manager who works on strategies to prevent youth violence for the whole student body. The grant covers calendar year 2022, and the grant period began before the Board's vote.

vendor.name: Sutter Bay Hospitals dba Alta Bates Summit Medical Center

items.fundingSource: Sutter Bay Hospitals dba Alta Bates Summit Medical Center

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

items.title: Grant Agreement - Sutter Bay Hospitals dba Alta Bates Summit Medical Center - Violence Prevention Program - Community Schools and Student Services Department

enrichment.headline: Extends La Clinica de la Raza's free dental care at Fremont High School's health center through June 2023
enrichment.summary: This is the second amendment to a memorandum of understanding (MOU) with La Clinica de la Raza. The clinic provides dental screening and treatment at the Tiger Health Center Clinic on the Fremont High School campus at no cost to the district. The stated period runs from July 1, 2019 through June 30, 2023, and all other terms stay the same.

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

items.title: Amendment No. 2, Memorandum of Understanding - La Clinica de la Raza - School-Based Health Centers - Community Schools and Student Services Department

enrichment.headline: Pays UC San Diego's pediatrics department up to $5,000 for medical advice to special education staff
enrichment.summary: The district contracts with the Regents of the University of California, through the UC San Diego School of Medicine's Department of Pediatrics, for two physicians to give medical consultation when district staff ask. Topics include students with special health care needs, when speech, occupational and physical therapy is medically necessary, and standing orders for emergency medications such as epinephrine. The Special Education Department manages it for July 1, 2022 through June 30, 2023, at no more than $5,000.

vendor.name: The Regents of the University of California (UC San Diego School of Medicine, Department of Pediatrics)

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

items.title: Services Agreement 2022-2023 - Regents of The University of California, San Diego School of Medicine, Department of Pediatrics – Special Education Department

enrichment.headline: Pays an Ohio-based contractor up to $90,000 to support students with complex medical needs
enrichment.summary: The district hires an individual based in Lyndhurst, Ohio to share information and work with district staff in support of students with complex medical needs whose ongoing treatment can make it hard to attend school. The Special Education Department manages the agreement for July 1, 2022 through June 30, 2023, at no more than $90,000.

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

items.title: Services Agreement 2021-2022 – Stacy Springer – Special Education Department

enrichment.headline: Pays a speech-language pathologist up to $115,200 to serve students with special education plans
enrichment.summary: The district contracts with an individual in San Leandro to work as a school-based speech-language pathologist. Duties include providing speech and language services to students with Individualized Education Programs (IEPs), attending IEP meetings, writing progress reports, Medi-Cal billing, assessments and case management. The Special Education Department manages it for July 1, 2022 through June 30, 2023, at no more than $115,200.

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

items.title: Services Agreement 2021-2022 – Rachel Hart – Special Education Department

enrichment.headline: Pays Holistic Speech Therapy up to $155,200 for speech and language services for special education students
enrichment.summary: The district contracts with Holistic Speech Therapy of Oakland to provide school-based speech and language services to students with Individualized Education Programs (IEPs). The work includes IEP meetings, progress reports, Medi-Cal billing, assessments and case management. The Special Education Department manages it for July 1, 2022 through June 30, 2023, at no more than $155,200.

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

items.title: Services Agreement 2021-2022 - Holistic Speech Therapy – Special Education Department

enrichment.headline: Pays STAC Physical Therapy Emeryville up to $90,000 to give students physical therapy at school
enrichment.summary: The district contracts with STAC Physical Therapy Emeryville, Inc. to deliver direct physical therapy to students in their learning environment, focusing on gross motor skills. The therapist also evaluates students, writes reports, builds treatment plans into each student's Individualized Education Plan and attends meetings. The Special Education Department manages it for July 1, 2022 through June 30, 2023, at no more than $90,000.

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

items.title: Services Agreement 2021-2022 – STAC Physical Therapy Emeryville, Inc. – Special Education Department

enrichment.headline: Accepts a $2.09M state Career Technical Education Incentive grant for the district's CTE programs
enrichment.summary: The district accepts a Career Technical Education Incentive Grant of $2,092,791 from the California Department of Education for its Career Technical Education program. The grant period is July 1, 2021 through December 31, 2023. The program is run by the High School Linked Learning Department.

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

items.title: Grant Award - California Department of Education - Career Technical Education Incentive - High School Linked Learning Department

enrichment.headline: Accepts a $4.13M state child care and development grant for the Early Childhood Education Department
enrichment.summary: The Board adopts a resolution approving a contract with the California Department of Education for the State General Child Care and Development Program. The district receives $4,127,761 for the program, which the Early Childhood Education Department runs. The contract covers July 1, 2022 through June 30, 2023.

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

items.title: Grant Award - California Department of Education - CCTR-2010 - Early Childhood Education Department

enrichment.headline: Lets Alameda County collect the district's 2022-23 bond and parcel taxes on property tax bills
enrichment.summary: The Board approves an agreement in which Alameda County collects the district's 2022-23 bond and parcel taxes on secured property tax bills. The district and the county agree to protect each other from certain claims (mutual indemnification). The text does not state a dollar amount.

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

items.title: Certification and Mutual Indemnification Agreement - County of Alameda - Collection of District Bond and Parcel Taxes - Fiscal Year 2022-2023

enrichment.summary: The Board adopts an amendment to its student policy on the COVID-19 vaccine requirement, Board Policy 5141.29. The agenda text says the changes are 'specified herein' but does not describe them, so the specific changes are not summarized here. No dollar amount is listed.

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

enrichment.summary: The Board approves a joint use agreement between the district and the Alameda County Office of Education for the property at 750 International Blvd. It covers July 1, 2020 through June 30, 2023, for a one-time payment of $44,373.12. enrichment.summary: The Board approves a tentative agreement between the district and AFSCME Local 257, a union of district employees. The agenda text does not describe the terms, what it costs, or how long it lasts.

enrichment.headline: Approves three tentative agreements with the teachers' union on early childhood programs for 2022-23
enrichment.summary: The Board approves three tentative agreements with the Oakland Education Association (OEA): a memorandum of understanding on a pilot for early childhood Teachers on Special Assignment, and two settlement agreements on itinerant teachers and expanding early childhood to a full day. Each runs from July 1, 2022 through June 30, 2023. Approval is pending compliance with state disclosure requirements, and no dollar amounts are given.

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

enrichment.summary: The Board ratifies the Board President's appointment of Andrew Butler, a parent or guardian of a child enrolled in the district, to the independent citizens' committee that oversees school facilities bond measures B, J and Y. enrichment.headline: Approves a no-cost partnership with EducationSuperHighway to help families sign up for internet
enrichment.summary: The district partners with EducationSuperHighway at no cost to help eligible families, with priority for unconnected families, enroll in the federal Affordable Connectivity Program for internet service. A related data sharing agreement lets the two share certain non-public information to carry out the enrollment help. Both run from July 1, 2022 through June 30, 2024.

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report
